plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Epigenetic Chromatin Switch & Twin Drift chart from Lyon (22 April 1961 Nature 190: 372–373), Allfrey, Faulkner & Mirsky (May 1964 PNAS 51: 786–794), Holliday & Pugh / Riggs (January 1975 Science 187: 226–232 & Cytogenet. Cell Genet. 14: 9–25), Waterland & Jirtle (August 2003 Mol. Cell. Biol. 23: 5293–5300), and Fraga & Esteller et al. (26 July 2005 PNAS 102: 10604–10609) compares active euchromatin (acetylated histone tails + unmethylated CpG islands = gene ON) against silenced heterochromatin (deacetylated histones + 5-methylcytosine CH3 tags + XIST Barr body = gene OFF), alongside Fraga & Esteller's 80-twin-pair comparison showing 3-year-old identical twins with near-identical profiles vs 50-year-old twins with 4x greater gene-expression divergence.

teach_overlay.label: HISTONE ACETYLATION (ON) VS CPG METHYLATION (OFF) · ESTELLER 2005 (80 TWIN PAIRS): 50-YR TWINS SHOW ~4× EPIGENETIC DIVERGENCE VS 3-YR TWINS
teach_overlay.detail: Inked chromatin switch & twin epigenetic drift chart on period paper showing histone tail acetylation (gene ON) vs cytosine CpG methylation (5mC, gene OFF) and comparing 80 monozygotic twin pairs (aged 3 to 74, Fraga & Esteller 2005 PNAS) where 50-year-old twins living apart show ~4x more differentially expressed genes and divergent 5mC/histone marks than 3-year-old twins
teach_overlay.scale: if your DNA sequence is the printed musical score of a symphony, epigenetic methyl and acetyl tags are the conductor's pencil marks — telling each cell which instruments to play loud and which to silence completely

plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period parchment, an inked Calico Cat X-Inactivation (Lyonization) mosaic map (from Barr & Bertram 1949 & Mary Lyon, 22 April 1961 Nature 190: 372–373) shows an early XX female cat embryo (~100–1,000 cells) where each cell randomly compacts either its orange-allele X chromosome or its black-allele X chromosome into an inactive Barr body coated in XIST RNA, growing into clonal patches of orange and black fur.

teach_overlay.label: 22 APR 1961 MARY LYON (NATURE): RANDOM XX INACTIVATION (50% PATERNAL / 50% MATERNAL BARR BODY) → CLONAL ORANGE & BLACK CALICO PATCHES
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Mary Lyon (22 April 1961 Nature 190: 372–373) X-chromosome dosage-compensation diagram showing random inactivation of 1 of 2 X chromosomes (50% paternal X / 50% maternal X compacted into a silent Barr body) in early female mammalian embryos, producing clonal orange-and-black coat mosaicism in XX calico females (while XY males are solid orange or black, with rare 1-in-3,000 XXY Klinefelter male calicos)
teach_overlay.scale: a female calico cat is a walking map of epigenetic switches — every orange patch on her coat is a family of skin cells that switched off the black X chromosome, and every black patch switched off the orange X chromosome
